title: 022 · Why? #10: completing the square with tiles, add 9; lowest value −9 (predict-first, white)

captions.instagram:
NDA Maths · Quadratic equations. x² + 6x: add what to make a perfect square? A 6 · B 9 · C 36 👇

B. Draw it: x² is a square, 6x is a strip. Split the strip in two (3x and 3x) and wrap it round the square.
One corner is missing: 3 × 3 = 9. So x² + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)².
Take the 9 back out: x² + 6x = (x + 3)² − 9. A square is never negative, so the lowest value is −9, at x = −3.
Traps: 6 just adds the middle number; 36 squares the 6 instead of half of it.

NDA asked it in 2026 (I), Q42: the minimum of x² + kx + k² = (x + k/2)² + 3k²/4, so 3k²/4.
